title: Invertibility and open restriction of a pullback tensor-power twist
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $L$ and $M$ be invertible modules on $X$ and $Y$, respectively [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $a\geq0$ put $N_a=L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f^*(M^{\otimes a})$, using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with $M^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_Y$. Then $M^{\otimes a}$, $f^*(M^{\otimes a})$ and $N_a$ are invertible. For every open $U\subseteq Y$, let $k:U\hookrightarrow Y$, $j:f^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_U:f^{-1}(U)\to U$ be the inclusions and restricted morphism, so $f\circ j=k\circ f_U$. There is an isomorphism of invertible $\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(U)}$-modules
$$N_a|_{f^{-1}(U)}\cong (L|_{f^{-1}(U)})\otimes f_U^*((M|_U)^{\otimes a}).$$
Here restriction is pullback along the open inclusion. The isomorphism is the composite of the pullback tensor comparison, the comparison of successive pullbacks along $f\circ j=k\circ f_U$, and the tensor-power comparison. In exponent zero the latter uses $f_U^*\mathcal O_U\cong\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(U)}$, whose tensor-formula map is $b\otimes c\mapsto b f_U^\sharp(c)$ with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. For each $U$ and $a$, the two modules in the displayed isomorphism are ample simultaneously [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No quasi-compactness, affine, finite-type or ampleness hypothesis is imposed on $f$ or $U$.

proof.text: Use the existing proved instances IsInvertible.tensorPow and IsInvertible.tensorObj in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.ProjectionFormula. The former inducts from the structure module at exponent zero, with successor M tensor M.tensorPow a. Pullback preserves invertibility by the proved instance IsInvertible.pullback, and transport along the inverse of boundaryPullbackComparison identifies ordinary pullback with the explicit tensor pullback. Apply this to M.tensorPow a along f, then tensor with L, and pull the twist back along j. These give the first three assertions and the invertibility of the left restricted twist.

For the degree-zero equation, expand only boundaryPullbackPowIso at zero. Its hom is the comparison from uniqueness of left adjoints followed by the ordinary pullback structure-module morphism. Apply the injective Hom equivalence of the normalized tensor-pullback adjunction. Naturality and homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app turn the composite into the ordinary adjunction unit followed by the pushforward of its structure-module morphism. Mathlib's pullbackPushforwardAdjunction_homEquiv_pullbackObjUnitToUnit identifies this with the structure-sheaf map. By definition tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit is the inverse image of that same map under the tensor adjunction. Thus the two morphisms agree. The tensor description is multiplication b tensor c maps to b h-sharp(c), and its inverse inserts one, by the balancing relation.

Use the already constructed invertibleTwistOpenRestrictionIso: compose boundaryPullbackTensorIso along j, the inverse tensorPullbackSectionComp along j and f, the equality j followed by f equals f_U followed by k, tensorPullbackSectionComp along f_U and k, and the pullback of boundaryPullbackPowIso along k. The recursive power comparison includes exponent zero, whose normalization was proved in the preceding step. All these are actual constructed isomorphisms, without additional invertibility or finiteness hypotheses.

Transport invertibility from the left restricted twist across invertibleTwistOpenRestrictionIso using IsInvertible.of_iso. With those two invertibility proofs as instances, apply isAmple_iff_of_iso to the same specified isomorphism. Choose that isomorphism as the existential witness, with the required equality given by reflexivity. No hypothesis excludes exponent zero, empty opens, or empty schemes.
